claims.statement: The frontend is a SvelteKit 2 / Svelte 5 SSR application built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-node, styled with Tailwind 4 and shadcn-svelte/bits-ui primitives, and charted with lightweight-charts; it exposes two interchangeable import aliases, SvelteKit's $lib/* and the shadcn-style @/*, both mapped to src/lib.

frontend/src/hooks.server.ts guards every request: it verifies the auth_token cookie with jose jwtVerify against JWT_SECRET using HS256, accepts only tokens whose scope is 'access' (deleting the cookie for anything else, including mfa_pending tokens), redirects unauthenticated non-/auth requests 303 to /auth/login, and redirects authenticated users away from /auth/login and /auth/signup to /.

A ?clear_session=true request to /auth/login or /auth/signup deletes any surviving auth_token cookie, sets locals.user to null, and renders the page instead of redirecting, which breaks the redirect loop caused by a stale cookie.

The root load (+layout.server.ts) returns { user: locals.user, sidebar_open, collapsed_watchlist_ids, watchlist_order } — no watchlist_sort. When locals.user is set it makes one getUserPreferencesService(fetch).getPreferences(token) call, copies each field across only after a shape check (boolean for sidebar_open, Array.isArray for collapsed_watchlist_ids and watchlist_order), and wraps the call in a try/catch that swallows failures so the defaults — sidebar_open true, empty collapsed ids, null order — are returned when the preferences endpoint is unreachable.

Authenticated pages follow a uniform server pattern: the load and each form action construct a client through the factory with SvelteKit's fetch and pass the raw auth_token as an explicit Authorization Bearer override, on ApiError 401 they delete the cookie and redirect 303 to /auth/login?clear_session=true, other statuses are re-thrown as SvelteKit error(status, message), and unknown failures become error(500, 'Internal Server Error').

The /security/[security_id] server load performs no data fetch: it reads the security_id param, throws error(400, 'Security ID is required') when it is absent, and otherwise returns { security_id } so the shell renders instantly. The security identity and its 1d price series are fetched after navigation by SecurityPageDataService (page-data.svelte.ts), which runs both getSecurity and getPrices in parallel inside Promise.all with getChartDateWindow(..., '1d') and treats an empty series as a successful load whose message lands in error.

Mutations use SvelteKit form actions that validate request.formData() and return fail(status, { message }) on ApiError; the shared EditableTitle component drives inline rename by posting to a named action or calling an onSave callback, using enhance from $app/forms. Login is the exception that writes the auth_token cookie directly (path '/', httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure outside dev, one-week maxAge) across its login, verify2fa, and passkeyLogin actions.

The abstract ApiClient base resolves its origin in one place — browser: VITE_API_BASE_URL or same-origin, server: VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL falling back to VITE_API_BASE_URL — strips a trailing slash, and appends /api/v1, so all client endpoints are relative to the versioned API root.

Every ApiClient request sets credentials: 'include', and an optional tokenOverride adds an Authorization Bearer header used for SSR where a server-to-server fetch does not forward the browser cookie. postFormData omits Content-Type so the multipart boundary is set by the browser, and delete returns undefined for a 204 response instead of parsing a body.

handleResponse throws ApiError for any non-ok response, and extractErrorMessage prefers the JSON detail field (FastAPI's shape), then message, then falls back to 'Request failed with status <status>'; the resulting message string is preserved so components can surface backend text directly.

Each API client module exports a factory getXxxService(customFetch?) alongside a default instance; SSR uses the factory so SvelteKit's load fetch is injected, while the default instance serves browser calls where the cookie is sent automatically.

The API layer covers separate backend areas with distinct clients: AccountClient (accounts, totals, holdings, sync, CSV), AccountService (cross-account holdings), AuthService (login, 2FA verify, passkey auth, signup, verify-email, logout, WS ticket), SecurityClient (/auth/2fa/* and /auth/passkeys/*), BrokerClient (/integration and /external), MarketService (search, prices, securities, watchlists including per-list sort and security reorder), PortfolioClient, UserPreferencesService, IndicatorsService, AlertsService, NotesService, DocumentsService, SnapshotsService, and AIService.

The route table covers a dashboard at /, account detail at /accounts/[id], the user-wide holdings view at /holdings, broker management at /brokers, watchlist management at /watchlists, security analysis at /security/[security_id], 2FA and passkey management at /settings/security, and the /auth/login, /auth/signup, /auth/logout, and /auth/verify-email auth routes, with /auth/verify-email's load reading the token query parameter and returning a success/error status. Only /, /accounts/[id], /brokers and /settings/security still await their data in the load; /holdings returns preferences only and /watchlists and /security/[security_id] return shell data without fetching.

Complex state and orchestration live in ES6 classes in *.svelte.ts files using runes ($state, $derived, $derived.by) rather than in .svelte components or legacy svelte/store: AccountsListState owns accounts, selection mode, groupBy, a SvelteSet of syncing account ids, and a record of per-account sync error messages, seeding from the SSR-provided accounts.
ModalState<T> in lib/utils/modal-state.svelte.ts is a reusable rune class exposing isOpen, data, open(), close(), and reset(), shared by every create/view/delete modal in the app.

+layout.svelte instantiates layout-scoped services at component init via setBrokerService(), setSecurityService(), and setWatchlistService(), which publish them with setContext under symbol keys; consumers call the matching getXxxService(), which returns the context instance, or — when given a customFetch — a fresh instance, while SecurityService alone additionally keeps a lazily created module-level defaultService reachable when setContext/getContext are unavailable outside a component hierarchy.

The state layer enforces hard rules: never destructure reactive primitives (it severs the Svelte 5 proxy and breaks reactivity), use $effect for side effects such as DOM listeners and starting a post-navigation load rather than for computing state or fetching data inline, and declare a property with $state if the whole reference will be reassigned since deep-proxied objects allow in-place mutation without redeclaration. Because $effect never runs during SSR, the post-navigation loads in +layout.svelte, /holdings and /security/[security_id] are deliberately placed in mount-time effects.

No module-level instantiated state class or raw exported $state may be exported from a .svelte.ts file, because in an SSR environment that bleeds one user's state into another user's request; the instance must be created in a component or layout and passed down through context.

Multi-step fetches are orchestrated inside a single service method rather than sequenced in a component: AccountsListState.syncAccount posts the sync request and then polls getSyncStatus until the account leaves the in-flight list, and WatchlistService.addSecurity short-circuits when the target list already holds that symbol/exchange, reuses a security id found anywhere in the loaded watchlists, only calls createOrUpdateSecurity when no id is found, and only then posts the membership request — the backend does not dedupe membership.

Services store real error message strings rather than a generic boolean error flag — BrokerService, WatchlistService, and SecurityService each expose an error string, and AccountsListState keeps a per-account syncErrors record — so the UI layer can render actionable feedback; all API calls in frontend tests must be mocked, since CI runs without a backend and an unmocked fetch fails the suite.

AccountsListState opens a WebSocket to /api/ws (URL derived from an absolute VITE_API_BASE_URL when present, otherwise from window.location) using a short-lived signed ticket from authService.getWsTicket(), maintains syncingAccountIds and syncErrors from the sync_started, sync_finished, and sync_failed event types, hydrates in-flight syncs from the sync-status endpoint on open, and reconnects on a 5-second timer after close.

syncAccount guards against lost pub/sub messages by polling the sync-status endpoint in waitForSyncFinish with a 60-second deadline, a 1.5-second interval, and a 5-second grace period after the account leaves the in-flight list, clearing the sync state and refetching accounts or setting a timeout error message.

The authenticated shell in +layout.svelte composes Sidebar.Provider bound to a sidebarOpen state seeded from data.sidebar_open inside untrack with onOpenChange wired to handleSidebarOpenChange, and AppSidebar plus Sidebar.Inset wrapping page content only when data.user is set; it instantiates the layout-scoped services, owns globalSearchOpen and globalSearchTargetWatchlist (published via setContext('toggleGlobalSearch') and setContext('openGlobalSearch')), renders GlobalSearch with bind:open and bind:targetWatchlist, and installs a document-level keydown handler for the modifier-free shortcuts /, w, h and 1-9/0 that prefetches each target before navigating.

AppSidebar is collapsible to icon size and stacks AppSidebarHeader (brand link to / plus the sidebar trigger), AppSidebarActions (a Search entry invoking the toggleGlobalSearch context callback with a / hint, a Watchlists link to /watchlists with a w hint and a Holdings link to /holdings with an h hint, both links built with resolve from $app/paths), AppSidebarWatchlist (renders every watchlist from getWatchlistService().watchlists as a collapsible group, not just the default one, with the 1-0 shortcut hint on default-list rows), AppSidebarProfile (footer dropdown reading the email from $page.data.user and navigating to /brokers, /settings/security, and a native POST form to /auth/logout), and a Sidebar.Rail whose centered chevron badge appears on hover and flips with sidebar.state.

GlobalSearch is a Command.Dialog bound to the layout's open state and to a $bindable targetWatchlist; it debounces marketService.search by 300 ms, groups results by security_type, and on select calls createOrUpdateSecurity then closes the dialog and gotos to /security/{id}. Its star button is target-aware: it resolves the bound target against the service's current watchlists, matches a result by symbol plus exchange, and either removes/adds membership on that target list or — with no target — looks the security up in defaultWatchlistSecurities and delegates to toggleSecurity, so an existing security is toggled rather than re-created. Closing the dialog resets the query, the results, and the bound target, and the /watchlists page's per-section '+' button opens it pre-targeted through the layout's openGlobalSearch context callback.

Type and money conventions: backend fields are mirrored as snake_case, list endpoints return PaginatedResponse<T> with an items array, and Money is { value?, units?, nanos?, currencyCode? } where moneyToNumber prefers units plus nanos/1e9 and falls back to parsing the string value while money() renders a localized dollar amount. Account holdings totals are nested as { cost: Money, value: Money }.

Account and institution domain enums live in lib/types/account.ts with getAccountTypeLabel and getInstitutionLabel helpers that accept an optional translate callback, and AccountHoldings extends PaginatedResponse<Holding> with account-level totals (total_value, total_profit_loss, total_profit_loss_percent, net_deposits, currency) consumed by the account detail header and the account-scoped holdings table.

Frontend tests use Vitest with jsdom and @testing-library/svelte configured in vite.config.ts (environment jsdom, url http://localhost/, setupFiles ./src/setupTest.ts, include src/**/*.test|spec), with setupTest.ts registering jest-dom, stubbing window.location, and deferring teardown ~50 ms so bits-ui body-scroll-lock timers do not throw after jsdom is destroyed; tests must mock every API client module and stub each method the component calls, and must also mock framework or third-party modules that reach the network or DOM ($app/forms, $app/paths, $app/navigation, $app/stores, lightweight-charts), replacing global.WebSocket in websocket tests.

hooks.server.test.ts runs under the node vitest environment, mocks $env/static/private, signs real HS256 tokens with jose for each case, and covers token-scope rejection such as mfa_pending tokens clearing the cookie while leaving locals.user null.

The frontend extension points are consistent: a new backend area is a class extending ApiClient exported as both a getXClient factory and a default instance; a new page is a +page.server.ts returning only the cheap slice it needs over a thin +page.svelte shell, keeping the standard 401-delete-and-redirect / ApiError-to-error shape for any read it does await, and deferring expensive reads to a page-owned rune service whose load() is started in a mount-time $effect with its returned error routed through redirectOn401; a new stateful feature is a Foo.svelte.ts rune class with isLoading and message-valued error state instantiated in the component that owns the state (as /holdings does with HoldingsService) or provided from +layout.svelte; and a new preference is a field added to UserPreferences in userPreferencesService.ts, patched from the component with patchPreferences, where shell-driving preferences are additionally read in +layout.server.ts's load behind a shape check inside the existing try/catch while page-scoped ones like holdings_table and holdings_group are read in that page's own +page.server.ts load inside a nested try/catch. A per-watchlist setting such as the security sort mode is not a preference but a watchlist field persisted through MarketService.

The /watchlists route's server load is inert: it returns { watchlists: [] } and never fetches, never reads and never deletes the auth cookie, because the layout-owned WatchlistService.loadWatchlists() is the single owner of the initial watchlist fetch; the empty array keeps the data.watchlists prop shape intact for the page's seeding guard, which is inert while the load stays empty.

The /watchlists page renders one section per watchlist with security links to /security/{id}, formatted price and daily-change pills, inline rename, a confirmation-modal delete, a per-watchlist sort dropdown wired to WatchlistService.setSort (which PATCHes the watchlist, not a preference), a Reorder mode with drag-and-drop, and per-list security reorder available only for custom-sorted lists. It reads the shared WatchlistService instance from context, seeding watchlistService.watchlists from its SSR data only when the service is still empty (now inert since the load returns []), and keeps watchlistOrder seeded from data or $page.data plus focus-driven per-watchlist row selection. moveWatchlist applies reorders optimistically and persists watchlist_order via patchPreferences, restoring both the service array and the local order snapshot and writing watchlistService.error when the patch fails. Its per-watchlist '+' button calls the layout's openGlobalSearch context callback with that watchlist.

WatchlistService is the single client-side owner of watchlist data: its constructor only wires getMarketService(customFetch), loadWatchlists(token) stores the array returned by GET /market/watchlists directly (each watchlist already carries its embedded securities) and resolves to null on success or the caught error on failure so callers can route a 401, defaultWatchlistSecurities is a $derived lookup for the Default list that backs hasSecurity and toggleSecurity (and therefore the id-less addToWatchlist/removeFromWatchlist shortcuts), and every write returning a WatchlistRead goes through replaceWatchlist(updated) which swaps one element by id while createWatchlist appends and deleteWatchlist filters. Failure handling differs per method: removeSecurityFromWatchlist, reorderSecurities and toggleSecurity re-run loadWatchlists in their catch and record the error only afterwards (the resync clears the shared error at its start), whereas removeSecurity, createWatchlist, renameWatchlist, setSort and addSecurityToWatchlist just record the message. reorderSecurities applies its new order optimistically before the PUT, setSort applies none because the response already carries the backend-ordered securities, and addSecurity is the multi-step resolve-or-create path.

Layout-level preferences are server-loaded and client-persisted in one round trip: sidebar_open, collapsed_watchlist_ids and watchlist_order are read in +layout.server.ts and written back with userPreferencesService.patchPreferences from the component owning the interaction (the layout's sidebar handler, AppSidebarWatchlist.toggleCollapsed, and the /watchlists reorder handler), always as fire-and-forget calls that only log on failure — except /watchlists, which restores its local snapshots and surfaces the message in watchlistService.error. Page-scoped holdings preferences follow the same write path but are read by the /holdings load: holdings_table and holdings_group feed holdings_table_config and group_mode, are patched through saveHoldingsTableConfig / saveHoldingsGroupMode, and their rejections are surfaced in a page-level persistError instead of only being logged. sidebar_watchlists is declared on UserPreferences but is not read by any component or load, and there is no watchlist_sort preference — per-watchlist sort is a WatchlistRead field persisted via PATCH /market/watchlists/{id}.

Watchlist ordering and collapse state are presentation layers over the shared service data: sortWatchlistsByOrder(watchlists, order) in watchlist-utils.ts sorts by index in the persisted id array and appends watchlists absent from it in their original relative order (declining to reorder at all when the order is null/empty), and sortSecurities(securities, sortKey) implements custom (ascending position), name_asc, name_desc, price_change_desc, price_change_asc, date_added and date_added_asc, falling back to the custom position order for any absent or unrecognised key. normalizeWatchlistSort narrows a persisted key to the WatchlistSort union, moveItem returns a fresh copy with one item shifted, and handleReorderKeydown is the shared ArrowUp/ArrowDown handler. AppSidebarWatchlist resolves watchlist_order and collapsed_watchlist_ids from a setContext seam first (the initialWatchlistOrder / initialCollapsedWatchlistIds keys used by app-sidebar.test-harness.svelte), then from $page.data, keeps collapse state in a SvelteSet, and persists the whole set on toggle; the /watchlists page applies the same helpers to the same service data.

WatchlistService models sort and membership order as server-owned per-watchlist state rather than a user preference: WatchlistRead carries a sort field of the WatchlistSort union (custom, name_asc, price_change_desc, price_change_asc, date_added, date_added_asc) plus each security's added_at and position. setSort persists through PATCH /market/watchlists/{id} and reorderSecurities through PUT /market/watchlists/{id}/securities/order with the given array order sent as-is, while MarketService still exposes the id-less default-list shortcuts POST/DELETE /market/watchlists/securities/{securityId} (addToWatchlist/removeFromWatchlist), the per-list POST/DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities/{securityId} (addSecurityToWatchlist/removeSecurityFromWatchlist), and the paginated GET /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities returning PaginatedResponse of SecuritySchema.

setupTest.ts additionally no-ops Element.prototype.scrollIntoView because bits-ui's Command calls it asynchronously on the active item and closest group heading, and suppresses only the DEV-only derived_inert console warning emitted by bits-ui's dismissible-layer afterSleep timers while forwarding every other warning.

The /holdings route has a single server load and no form actions, and it deliberately awaits only the cheap preferences-derived keys so the page shell renders instantly: it normalizes holdings_table and holdings_group, forwards elliott_waves, and returns { holdings_table_config, group_mode, elliott_waves } — it never calls getUserHoldings. getUserPreferencesService(fetch).getPreferences(token) is wrapped in a try/catch so a preference failure is non-fatal and renders the default table config, flat group mode and null waves; because the load performs no authenticated read, it has no 401 redirect path.

AccountService covers both holdings scopes: getHoldings(securityId) reads the per-security account breakdown at /accounts/holdings/{securityId}, and getUserHoldings(offset = 0, limit = 50, token?) reads the user-wide paginated GET /accounts/holdings?offset=&limit= typed as PaginatedResponse<UserHolding>, passing the same optional SSR token override that factory-built clients use.

The /holdings page instantiates its own HoldingsService at component init, seeds groupBy from data.group_mode (so toggling grouping re-renders from memory instead of refetching), and starts service.load() from a mount-time $effect whose returned error is passed to redirectOn401; groupBy is a rune and groupedHoldings is a $derived.by over groupHoldings(rows, mode) from lib/utils/finance/holdings-group.ts. It renders components/holdings/holdings-table.svelte from service.rows. The same module exports setHoldingsService() / getHoldingsService(customFetch?) under Symbol('holdings-service'), where the customFetch call returns an isolated instance, but no production component reads that context.

HoldingsService.load(token) is the client-side path that now actually supplies the /holdings rows: it pages getUserHoldings with PAGE_SIZE 50 until offset >= total or an empty page, capped at MAX_PAGES 100 as a stale-total safety valve, accumulates every page into a collected array before assigning rows so a component never sees a half-paginated portfolio, keeps the previous rows when a page rejects, returns the caught error (null on success) so the page can route a 401 through redirectOn401, and stores the thrown message (Error message or String(error)) in errorMessage.

UserHolding in lib/types/account.ts is Holding extended with account_id and account_name, mirroring the backend UserHoldingRead returned by the user-wide GET /accounts/holdings; it is the row type of the /holdings table (HoldingsTable receives UserHolding rows and HoldingsService.rows is typed UserHolding[]), which is what lets that view render an Account column and aggregate one stock across accounts.

UserPreferences in lib/api/userPreferencesService.ts carries the holdings preferences holdings_table (HoldingsTableConfig from components/holdings/holdings-table-columns) and holdings_group (HoldingsGroupMode from lib/utils/finance/holdings-group) alongside the sidebar, watchlist, chart and holdings_period fields, plus indicator_pane_heights, and the same module re-exports the Elliott-wave, Fibonacci and drawing persistence shapes declared under $lib/utils/finance/ that consumers use to type a preference payload without importing the math modules directly.

Holdings are rendered by two independent, route-scoped tables with no shared component between them: /accounts/[id] feeds the older components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte from an SSR AccountHoldings payload, while /holdings feeds components/holdings/holdings-table.svelte from UserHolding rows plus tableConfig, groupBy, elliottWaves and an onConfigChange callback that the page uses to persist column changes.

frontend/src/lib/api/async-data.ts defines redirectOn401, the single seam for post-navigation load failures: it gotos to /auth/login?clear_session=true when the error is an ApiError with status 401 and returns true (the caller must then stop and not render its own error state), and returns false for any other error so the caller surfaces the message in its own in-page alert. The httpOnly auth_token cookie is not deleted client-side — the clear_session query param makes hooks.server.ts clear it server-side — and the convention enabling this is that post-navigation service methods return the caught error instead of throwing (WatchlistService.loadWatchlists, HoldingsService.load and SecurityPageDataService.load all resolve to null on success or the error on failure).

The layout's watchlists effect is the single owner of the initial watchlist fetch and the shortcut prefetch pass: after hydration, when data.user is set, it awaits watchlistService.loadWatchlists() (returning early through redirectOn401 on error) and on success warms the 1-9/0 shortcut targets in order — /watchlists, /holdings, then the first ten defaultWatchlistSecurities — via preloadData(resolve(url)) through a prefetchUrl helper that records each URL in a per-component-instance SvelteSet so a target is prefetched at most once and a rejected prefetch is swallowed. The same prefetchUrl is reused by the keyboard handler's w, h and numeric shortcuts so the target is warmed before goto.

The route-level test suites are per-page pairs that pin the shell-first split without a running server: routes/holdings/page.server.test.ts mocks $lib/api/accountService and $lib/api/userPreferencesService and asserts the load returns exactly the three preference keys and that getUserHoldings was never called; routes/holdings/page.svelte.test.ts mocks the same two modules plus $app/paths and $app/navigation and renders the page with a data prop to drive grouping, column visibility and per-currency totals; routes/security/[security_id]/page.server.test.ts asserts the load returns only security_id, never calls getSecurity or getPrices, and throws 400 without the param; routes/watchlists/page.server.test.ts asserts the load returns { watchlists: [] }, never fetches, and neither reads nor deletes the cookie; routes/watchlists/page.svelte.test.ts mocks the market client and preferences service while keeping a real WatchlistService instance (mocking only getWatchlistService) and injecting openGlobalSearch through render context so the page's $derived ordering and sorting run against real rune state; and routes/layout.test.ts renders +layout.svelte with a createRawSnippet child, capturing the context WatchlistService in the snippet's setup, to assert the unauthenticated bare-children path versus the Sidebar.Provider path, the keyboard shortcuts, the prefetch order and its failure swallowing, and the +layout.server.ts load defaults.
